standard_prerequisites.name: The Gallai-Edmonds decomposition (D, A, C) of a graph, its parameters r and h, and the components D_i of G[D]
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's subsection on the Edmonds-Gallai decomposition (source lines 1054-1098), where the parameters r and h are defined
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes every symbol that appears in the identity, in particular the sets A, C, D, their sizes a, r, and the quantity h.

core_obligations: Degree summation on the D part: summing the degrees of the vertices of D expresses d|D| through the internal edges of the components, the edges between different components and the edges from D to A and to C (proof lines 1106-1109).
Rearrange for h: since h is the sum of the inter-component edges of G[D] and the edges from D to C, the author obtains 2h = d|D| - 2 sum_i e_G(D_i) - e_G(D,A) + e_G(D,C) (proof lines 1110-1113).
Degree summation on the A part: summing degrees over A gives d|A| = 2e_G(A) + e_G(A,D) + e_G(A,C) (proof lines 1114-1117).

Combine the two identities: subtracting the A identity from the D identity and substituting the Gallai-Edmonds relations |D| - |A| = r + sum over components of size at least three of (|D_i| - 1) and 2e_G(D_i) = d|D_i| - e_G(D_i, D_i^c), the author proves the claimed identity, combining the sums because every |D_i| is odd (proof lines 1118-1127).
proof_roadmap: 对 D 求和：d|D| = 2 sum_i e_G(D_i) + 2 sum_{i<j} e_G(D_i,D_j) + e_G(D,A) + e_G(D,C)，解出 h。
对 A 求和：d|A| = 2e_G(A) + e_G(A,D) + e_G(A,C)。
两式相减，再代入 Gallai-Edmonds 的两个关系式 |D|-|A| = r + sum_{|D_i|>=3}(|D_i|-1) 与 2e_G(D_i) = d|D_i| - e_G(D_i,D_i^c)，由每个 |D_i| 为奇数把两项求和合并，得到要证的恒等式。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the exact edge-counting identity for the Gallai-Edmonds parameters (author lemma at source lines 1099-1103, whose statement is the author's own display eq:ge-exact). The proof (source lines 1105-1127) is a two-sided degree summation: it sums degrees over the D part to relate the parameter h to the internal, inter-component and boundary edges (proof lines 1106-1113), sums degrees over A (proof lines 1114-1117), and then substitutes the two structural relations of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition, using the oddness of the component sizes to merge the two sums into one (proof lines 1118-1127). The identity is what makes the later probabilistic estimates on the decomposition quantitative, and the proof has to keep track of which edges are counted twice. H2.
